fi-danio-albolineatus.title: Pearl Danio
fi-danio-albolineatus.summary: The pearl danio, Danio albolineatus, is a small cyprinid recorded from Myanmar and Indochina south to Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra. Colour and patterning differ between localities, and doubts…
rows: schooling species by nature and really should be kept in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Stomach analyses of wild specimens have revealed this species to be chiefly insectivorous, feeding on a variety of aquatic/terrestrial insects and their larvae.
Currently understood to be widely-distributed with records existing from parts of Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Peninsular Malaysia and the Indonesian island of Sumatra .
notes: Looks particularly effective in a heavily-planted arrangement with a darker substrate, and may appear paler in sparsely-decorated set-ups.
We suggest maintaining it in a well-planted aquarium or set-up designed to resemble a flowing river or stream, with a substrate of variably-sized rocks and gravel and some large water-worn boulders.

fi-danio-rerio.title: Zebra Danio
fi-danio-rerio.summary: The zebra danio, Danio rerio, is a small cyprinid from India and Bangladesh, found mostly in slow or still pools and mature rice paddies. Peaceful, hardy and inexpensive, it has been mass-produced…
rows: schooling species by nature and should be maintained in a group of at least 8-10 specimens.
Omnivore. Stomach analyses of wild specimens have shown it to be a micropredator, feeding on aquatic crustaceans and other invertebrates such as mosquito larvae.
Described from the Kosi River, a tributary of the Ganges system in Uttar Pradesh state, northern India.
notes: Choice of décor is not especially critical though it tends to show better colouration in a heavily-planted set-up with a dark substrate.
The addition of some floating plants and driftwood roots or branches to diffuse the light entering the tank also seems to be appreciated and adds a more natural feel.
